ship-mark.title: The Ship Mark
ship-mark.start: Someone who wore your ship's mark came to Lumar long before you did.
ship-mark.done: A pilot of your line came here, met the dragon, and never left. Whatever they were listening for, the egg is listening for it too.

clues.text: A skeleton deep in the dragon's cave clutches a medal. The ship mark on it is yours.
In the sorceress's tower, a scroll sealed in red wax. The seal bears the same ship mark.
The tavern's oil painting: a ship under a full green moon, signed 'E.B.'
A traveller's compass at the inn that never settles on north.
The inn's guestbook, last entry, no name: 'The dragon is not asleep. It is listening.'
The dragon's egg glows faintly. Something inside is listening.

letter.text:
Heard you went down into the dragon's cave and came back up. Nobody does that.

So it was one of yours, all those years back. E.B. sat at my table every night for a season and never once said what they were listening for. I'm glad somebody finally went looking.

The painting stays on the wall. Drink's on me when you're next in.

Bram

heron.title: The Heron's Cargo
heron.start: A galleon called the Heron broke her back on the Crimson reef. Somebody thinks her cargo is still aboard.
heron.done: H.M. charted the reef, hid the chart on the stack and went for the cargo through the dragon's caves. The pirates are waiting for the tide to do the same.

clues.text: A chest under an X on the sea stack: a reef chart and a note. 'The Heron's cargo is still aboard. - H.M.'
The Heron lies listing on the reef, her hold open to the sea.
In the pirates' tent, the same reef chart, the wreck circled twice.
Charcoal by the cave mouth, signed H.M.: 'Down the stairs, bear left, mind the lava.'
The Crimson Watcher keeps the camp's fire and tells you to keep away from the cave.

letter.text:
The tide turned last night and the pirates went out to the Heron with their ropes and their lamps, and came back with nothing but wet boots. You'd been there first. I watched it all from the fire.

H.M. would have liked you, I think. Mind the reef.

Corra

signal.title: Forty-Seven Point Three
signal.start: Enigma's antenna is still listening to something on 47.3 MHz.
signal.done: Okafor never left. The missing suit, the bedroll, the lantern, the drone tuned to the signal: someone is still aboard Enigma, answering it.

clues.text: The antenna array: signal detected on 47.3 MHz, source unknown, still listening.
The data core's logs: contact with command lost 72 cycles ago. 'No one is coming.'
The bay log: the skiff Wren left in 4402 and never returned. Okafor started repairs on the Kestrel.
Four hooks, three suits. The empty one is D. Okafor's.
A bedroll in Docking Bay 3. The lantern beside it is still lit.
A maintenance drone on the bench, tuned to 47.3 MHz.

letter.text:
Skyport 7 to the Wayfarer.

That station you've been poking round, Enigma: we logged a crew list for it, years back. One name never came off the board. Sounds like you found out why.

Pad seven's yours whenever you want it. No landing fee.

Ruiz

brink.title: Echoes at the Brink
brink.start: Time runs wrong at the Brink. Things that happened elsewhere happen here too.
brink.done: Every echo at the Brink is of somewhere you have been. The hole isn't remembering the universe. It's remembering you.

clues.text: A sundial with no sun, its shadow pointing at the hole and growing.
A half-sunk ring of stone. Through it the stars are in the wrong places, and you can see your own back.
Steps that climb into nothing, the last few hanging loose and turning slowly.
An echo of Lumar: cobbles from a square you know, a lantern still burning, half a wall.
An echo of Arcadia: a slab of street still wet with rain that fell somewhere else.
An echo of a station: a server rack blinking the same pattern Enigma was transmitting.
A rockfall stopped mid-air. If you watch long enough, one stone moves.

letter.text:
You went to the edge and it showed you yourself. They all say it shows them the universe. It doesn't. It shows them where they've been, and most people haven't been anywhere.

You have. Keep going.

The back corner, as ever

null.title: NULL
null.start: Somebody has been spraying NULL around the District.
null.done: NULL is a crew. The broken cabinet is their drop, the kid runs their messages, and Club Void is where they meet. The chained gate is where they live.

clues.text: The alley gate, chained shut. Someone sprayed NULL on the bars.
A broken arcade cabinet flickers fragments of something hidden.
A stranger in the arcade: the old owner left something inside that broken cabinet.
The street kid asks for tokens, and watches the gate.
Club Void. A slot in the door opens, two eyes, and closes again.

letter.text:
ok so you know about us now. dont tell joro. the gate stays chained, thats the rule, but if you ever need something run anywhere in the district, you know who to ask. tokens up front.

P

(this is a NULL letter. burn it)

crystals.title: Four Colours
crystals.start: The cartographer says each of Lumar's four islands grows its own colour of crystal.
crystals.done: Crimson, rose, sapphire, and whatever the stones on Midnight are guarding. The cartographer will want to hear it.

clues.text: The cartographer: four islands, four colours of crystal. Three mapped. Nobody maps Midnight.
Crimson crystals in a field above the reef, all leaning toward the ridge.
Rose crystals, harvested on Rose Cove.
Sapphire crystals, traded at Sapphire Port.
On Midnight Isle, stone sentinels guard the way to the sorceress's tower.

letter.text:
Four colours, as I thought - and the Midnight stones guarding a fourth that nobody has ever drawn.

I've added all of them to the chart, with your name in the corner where the cartographer usually signs. It's only fair. Come by the house and see it: the ink's barely dry.

Ilsa Venn

wren.title: The Wren
wren.start: Okafor has been listening to the same distress loop for seventy-two cycles. It's getting clearer.
wren.done: The Wren was waved off at Arcadia and spent its last burn going toward the dark. It reached the Brink and is still there, nose-first over the edge, falling so slowly it looks still. The loop Okafor hears is its call, slowed by the hole, only now climbing out.

clues.text: Dami Okafor, the engineer who stayed, in a garden off the relay deck.
The radio: "Wren to Enigma. We can see the edge. We are not afraid."
Five crew in flight jackets in front of a skiff called Wren. Okafor in the corner of every photo.
Marshal Ruiz waved the Wren off Skyport 7 in a storm. It turned toward the dark side.
At the Brink, a piece of Enigma's hull, its lights blinking the station's pattern.
The Wren itself, past the altar at the very edge, frozen mid-fall. Its running lights are on.

letter.text:
Seventy-two cycles I listened to that loop, and you went and found them in a week.

I keep thinking of the Wren out there, nose over the edge, still falling. Still calling. At least now I know the call's not for help. It's just them saying where they are.

The tomatoes say hello.

Dami Okafor

listeners.title: The Listeners
listeners.start: The monks of Midnight Isle kept a record of every ship that passed. The record is gone.
listeners.done: The monks listened to the sky from the moon pool and wrote down the ships they heard overhead - starships, on a sea world. Morwen keeps their book. Its last page names the Wren, and after it a skiff that hadn't been built yet. Yours.

clues.text: The abbey ruins: the monks kept a record of every ship that passed. The book is gone.
Carved over the tomb door, violet light inside: "THEY LISTENED TOO."
In the moon pool, a full green moon that isn't in the sky.
The graveyard of the drowned. One stone is new and still blank.
Through Morwen's telescope: something dark moving between the stars.
Morwen has the monks' book. She knows what's on the last page.

letter.text:
The book is open on my table to its last page, and I find I can't close it. The Wren, and then your skiff, written in a hand three hundred years dead.

The monks heard you coming before you were built. I don't know what that means yet. When I do, you'll have a letter.

Morwen

keepsakes.title: Five Berths
keepsakes.start: The Wren's crew left their berths in Enigma's ring exactly as they were the day they flew.
keepsakes.done: A harmonica, a short deck of cards, a pressed flower, a letter nobody finished, a child's drawing. They all meant to come back. Okafor should know someone has seen them.

clues.text: Ada's harmonica, worn bright where her thumbs went: 'For the long hauls.'
Bix's cards, fifty-one of them. The ace of hearts is missing: 'I'll win it back.'
Cora, the medic, kept a pressed Lumar spore-bloom. It still glows.
Dell's unfinished letter: he swapped a shift so Dami could finish her tug.
Eze, the youngest, flew the Wren. A drawing from home: 'Big sister Eze flies the Wren.'

letter.text:
You went down to the ring. I haven't, not since. I couldn't make my feet do it.

Dell's letter - I knew he'd swapped for me. I didn't know he'd written it down. I'm going to finish it for him and send it to his sister. Mar should know he was laughing that morning.

Thank you for looking at their things like they mattered. They did.

Dami

keepers-log.title: Three Long, One Short
keepers-log.start: The Sapphire Light never goes out, but nobody in the port has seen its keeper in weeks.
keepers-log.done: Thirty years ago the Morning Tide didn't come home, and a light on Midnight Isle answered the lighthouse with her call sign. Three weeks ago it started answering again. Tamsin Gale hasn't left the lamp since; she answers it every night, so whoever's out there knows where home is.

clues.text: Three weeks of the same entry in the keeper's log: a light answering from Midnight, north by east. Three long, one short.
Thirty years back, the night the Morning Tide was lost, the old keeper logged the same signal from Midnight - and never wrote of it again.
A cut sapphire set in the lens turns the beam blue. Scratched beside it: 'So they know it's us.'
Someone has been answering from up here, every night. Three long, one short: the Morning Tide's call.
Tamsin Gale keeps the light. Her mother skippered the Morning Tide.

letter.text:
The light answered again last night, and for the first time in three weeks I went to bed after. Slept till noon. The clock ran down, the lens stopped, and the sky didn't fall in.

I wound it back up, mind.

If you're ever north by east of us after dark, flash three long and one short. I'll know it's you.

Tamsin Gale
Keeper, the Sapphire Light

singing-deep.title: The Singing Deep
singing-deep.start: Somewhere deep in the old Rose Mine, something is singing.
singing-deep.done: Twenty floors down, under the cold and the blue stone, the great songstone sang its one long note. You broke it open and took its heart - and the whole mine sang back. Hob says it's the first time in forty years he's heard it change key.

clues.text: The Rose Mine. The timbers are old but sound, and from somewhere deep inside comes a sound like singing.
The foreman's slate counts down the floors: blue at five, cold at ten, 'don't linger' at fifteen - and a question mark at twenty.
Hob Dunmore, the last miner, says the singing started the winter they opened floor twenty. Nobody has been down to see what it is.
At the bottom of the mine, the great songstone - a crystal the size of a cart, singing one long note.

letter.text: IT'S QUIET DOWN THERE NOW, BUT NOT SILENT - MORE LIKE IT'S LISTENING. I WENT DOWN TO FIFTEEN YESTERDAY FOR THE FIRST TIME IN TWENTY YEARS. BRING ME SOME STAR IRON SOMETIME AND I'LL MAKE YOU SOMETHING WORTH CARRYING. - HOB

queens-favour.title: The Queen's Favour
queens-favour.start: Queen Alyssara asked you, quietly, to find the ribbon Beckolas lost from his sword.
queens-favour.done: The queen's favour is back on her first sword's hilt. Beckolas owes you one, and he is the sort to remember it.

clues.text: The queen tied a ribbon to Beckolas's sword, green silk worked with gold leaves. He's lost it and is too proud to tell her. She knows anyway.
The bard is already writing a song about it: the first sword at the Moonwell, a gust of wind, a ribbon gone up into the willow.
At dawn the herbalist saw Beckolas climbing the willow by the Moonwell in full armour, and climbing down again with nothing.
With what the bard and the herbalist told you, you know where to look: high in the willow over the Moonwell, caught on a frond, a ribbon of green silk with gold leaves. You climb up and free it.
You hand Beckolas the ribbon. He ties it back on his sword without a word, then bows to you, very low. On the throne, the queen pretends not to notice, and smiles.

letter.text:
Traveller.

I am not good at letters. The queen says that is obvious and to write it anyway.

Thank you for the ribbon. You could have told the whole glade. You told no one, and you gave it to me to give back. That was kind, and I don't forget kindness.

If you are ever in Elderglade and in trouble, say my name. Loudly. I will come.

Beckolas, first sword of the queen

under-the-willow.title: Under the Willow
under-the-willow.start: The queen loves her first sword, her first sword loves the queen, and the whole wood knows it except, possibly, the two of them. She's asked you to help. Gently.
under-the-willow.done: Under the willow at dusk, the first sword finally said it. Faelan's lanterns and Sefa's ribbons are staying up in the willow for good.

clues.text: The queen confided in you: she loves Beckolas, and she's fairly sure he loves her, but a sworn sword won't speak above his oath and a queen can't command a heart. She asked you to find out. Gently. He bruises like a peach.
Beckolas denied everything, turned the colour of a sunset, then admitted it: three hundred years, two hundred and twelve attempts to tell her, and one letter he wrote, panicked over and ate.

Thaelin has had the song written for a century. He agrees Beckolas has to say it himself, and he knows where: the Moonwell at dusk, where everyone says the true thing. He'll be in the bushes. Playing very quietly.
Mirelle gave you a moonflower she's kept for Beckolas for twenty years. It only opens in the hand of someone who means what they're about to say.
Faelan will light the willow over the Moonwell at dusk with the good lanterns. He's been saving them six hundred years for something worth lighting.
Sefa will tie the willow with ribbons of the same green silk as Beckolas's favour. She wove a whole bolt of it in the spring. She knew. Everyone knew.
You gave Beckolas the moonflower and told him: the Moonwell, at dusk. He went pale, said nothing for a long time, then went off to polish his armour. All of it. Twice.
You told the queen: the Moonwell, at dusk. She said she would be very surprised, and went to find a different circlet.
At dusk under the lit willow Beckolas held out the moonflower, and it opened in his hand. He said it all in one breath. The queen said "Finally."
clues.say:
THE WILLOW IS FULL OF LANTERNS AND GREEN RIBBONS, AND THE MOONWELL IS FULL OF THEIR LIGHT. BECKOLAS IS ALREADY HERE, IN VERY SHINY ARMOUR.

THE QUEEN COMES DOWN THE PATH. HE OPENS HIS MOUTH, CLOSES IT, AND HOLDS OUT THE MOONFLOWER. IT OPENS IN HIS HAND.

"I LOVE YOU," HE SAYS, ALL IN ONE BREATH. "I HAVE FOR THREE HUNDRED YEARS. I'M SORRY IT TOOK SO LONG. I ATE A LETTER ABOUT IT ONCE."

THE QUEEN TAKES THE FLOWER. "FINALLY," SHE SAYS, AND KISSES HIM.

SOMEWHERE IN THE BUSHES, A LUTE PLAYS VERY QUIETLY.
